To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the critical Rayleigh numbers of the secondary flow are smaller than that of the horizontal flow, (ii) the preferred flow pattern of the secondary flow is the same as that of the horizontal one, (iii) the preferred shape of the upper boundary of the dendrite layer is the same as the preferred flow pattern, (iv) the preferred flow and the preferred shape of upper boundary are both caused by the temperature variation of the secondary flow and (v) the preferred flow patterns are
the secondary flow in the dendrite layer is found to be unstable in the absence of rotation and stable in the presence of rotation.
the preferred flow pattern is the same as that found for the case of a flat upper boundary and the preferred shape of the upper boundary is the same as the preferred horizontal flow pattern.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mathematical modeling, nonlinear features and stability of the secondary flow in a horizontal dendrite solidification layer.
the stability of the secondary flow in the dendrite layer in the presence of rotation.
the stability of secondary flow and the effect of rotation on the flow in the dendrite layer, and the effect of the deformed boundary of the layer on the solidification process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the secondary flow is stable and its preferred flow pattern is the same as that of the primary flow.
the secondary flow is a result of the interaction of the primary flow and the temperature variations of both the primary flow and secondary flow.
the secondary flow is a preferred flow pattern in the dendrite layer and it is the most important flow pattern in the layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a stable flow pattern is obtained when the upper boundary is deformed to be convex upward.
the secondary flow in the dendrite layer is found to be stable for all the values of the parameters used in the present study.
a preferred flow pattern is detected in the dendrite layer, which can be considered as a new flow pattern.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a secondary flow can lead to an enhanced stability of the system.
the presence of the deformed boundary and the rotation of the layer have stabilizing effects on the flow and the solidification process.
the preferred shape of the upper surface of the dendrite layer is a result of the interaction between the secondary flow and the temperature variations within the dendrite.
